The exit code is there because the program must also still run. ★★ THE MEASURED AXIS IS THE DECLARATOR SHAPE, NOT THE ATTRIBUTE. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-03, four attributes (`deprecated`, `nodiscard`, `maybe_unused`, `noreturn`) x two declarator shapes, each reference probed SEPARATELY: a C23 `[[...]]` run written after a declarator appertains to the ENTITY when the declarator is a bare identifier and to the array-or-function TYPE when it derives one, and the answer is constant across the four attributes. `int x [[deprecated]];` -- gcc 13.3.0 warns at the USE, clang 18.1.3 warns at the USE, MSVC 19.51 /std:clatest C4996 at the USE. `int arr[3] [[deprecated]];` and `void f(void) [[deprecated]];` -- gcc `'deprecated' attribute ignored`, clang `error: 'deprecated' attribute cannot be applied to types` (rc=1), MSVC `C4649 attributes are ignored in this context`. C23 6.7.6p1 vs 6.7.6.2p1/6.7.6.3p1 is why. The GNU spelling has NO such split (✔MEASURED, it confers on the entity in every declarator shape in gcc and clang; MSVC implements no `__attribute__` at any /std: and ABSTAINS), which is why the grain is declared PER RULE. ★★★ AND THIS IS WHY NARROWING ONE LOOP WOULD HAVE TRADED ONE DEFECT FOR ANOTHER: ✔MEASURED at base `6482a71b` through the shipped CLI, DSS conferred on BOTH `void f(void) [[deprecated]];` (above the union -- NO reference confers) and `int x [[deprecated]];` (correct -- ALL THREE confer), out of the same over-broad read.
